newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar energy delegation to Japan for gas talks.
newsitem.headline: Qatar energy delegation to Japan for gas talks.

text.p: Qatar's Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah will head a Qatari gas delegation to Japan from September 28, an official at the state-owned Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) said on Sunday.

Meetings will include talks with Japanese firms interested in taking an equity stake in Qatar's second liquefied natural gas (LNG) project -- the Ras Laffan LNG Company (Rasgas) -- and potential Japanese buyers of Qatari gas.
Sumitomo Corp, Itochu and Nissho Iwai are seeking a 10 percent stake in Rasgas, currently 70 percent owned by QGPC and 30 percent by Mobil Corp.
"We are not sure if any decision will be taken in this matter, but it cannot be ruled out either," the Qatari official said on the proposed stake deal.
Rasgas chairman Yousef Hussain Kamal will be part of the Qatari delegation to Japan.
Qatari officials are also keen to secure additional long-term gas supply deals with Japanese power generators, gas marketers and traders.
"The visit is very crucial for Qatar, as several Japanese buyers are waiting to meet the minister to hold talks on purchase of LNG from the Rasgas project," the official said.
Japan and South Korea are being earmarked as the main market for Qatari LNG.
Chubu Electric Power Co begins lifting an annual four million tonnes a year of gas from the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas) from December under a 25-year supply deal.
Mitsui and Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp each have a 7.5 percent stake in Qatargas which is designed to produce six million tonnes a year for the Japanese market.
Al-Attiyah will also attend the naming of the first LNG vessel, the Al Zubarah, for exporting the gas to Japan at the Chiba dockyard on October 4.
